'''Yasha Asley''' is a British mathematics [[child prodigy]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 March 2017 |title=Teen genius dubbed 'human calculator' becomes UK university lecturer at 14 |work=Al Arabiya English |url=https://english.alarabiya.net/features/2017/03/31/Teen-genius-dubbed-human-calculator-becomes-UK-university-lecturer-at-14-}}</ref> of Iranian descent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nuzat |first=Safoora |date=1 April 2017 |title=Meet Iran's Yasha, 'worlds youngest professor' in UK |url=https://archive.siasat.com/news/meet-irans-yasha-worlds-youngest-professor-uk-1164436/ |access-date=4 November 2022 |website=Siasat}}</ref>

==Life== 
Raised solely by his father, Moussa, Yasha was gifted at maths from an early age.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} When he started [[primary school]] at the age of four, he was described as having the mathematical ability of a typical twelve-year-old.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bright Sparks: Child prodigy Yasha got a First Class Maths degree at 15 years old {{!}} ITV New|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkSPmWH3zBQ|last=|first=|date=24 July 2018|website=[[YouTube]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009132719/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkSPmWH3zBQ|archive-date=9 October 2020|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=14 Year Old Child Prodigy Hired by University of Leicester As Math Teacher|url=https://www.universityherald.com/articles/70116/20170322/child-prodigy-hired-by-university-as-math-teacher-at-fourteen.htm|last=Herald|first=University|date=2017-03-22|website=University Herald|language=en|access-date=2020-05-16|archive-date=22 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181122215705/https://www.universityherald.com/articles/70116/20170322/child-prodigy-hired-by-university-as-math-teacher-at-fourteen.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> While attending school Asley passed the [[A-level]] exams and became the youngest person to have achieved the 'A' grade in Mathematics at the age of 8 in 2011, surpassing a record previously held by [[March Tian Boedihardjo]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2011-03-30|title=Boy, 8, gets A in A-level maths|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-12852989|access-date=2020-05-16|archive-date=11 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111214251/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-12852989|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/hampshire/7941327.stm |title=Boy, 8, sets A-level maths record |work=BBC News |date=13 March 2009 |access-date=8 February 2019 |archive-date=4 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104212258/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/hampshire/7941327.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

For three years prior to starting his university education his full-time schooling was split, three days a week at primary school and two days a week he learned mathematics with Professor [[Alexander Gorban]] at the [[University of Leicester]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2011-03-30|title=Boy, 8, gets A in A-level maths|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-12852989|access-date=2020-05-16|archive-date=11 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111214251/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-12852989|url-status=live}}</ref>

Although he had met UK university entrance requirements by scoring top grades and was in a position to apply to UK universities, he wanted to continue in the standard education system.  In an ITV interview, on 24 July 2018, Yasha said, "... It wasn't our first choice [to go to university]. But then it seemed like the headteacher had told my teachers to slow me down... So we decided that I really had no choice [other than to go to university]." He began his university course at the age of twelve.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bright Sparks: Child prodigy Yasha got a First Class Maths degree at 15 years old {{!}} ITV News|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkSPmWH3zBQ|last=|first=|date=|website=[[YouTube]]|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009132719/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XkSPmWH3zBQ|archive-date=9 October 2020|access-date=}}</ref>

In 2017, at the age of 15, he became the university's youngest-ever graduate receiving a first-class degree in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=15-year-old graduates from university with first-class degree|url=https://www.itv.com/news/central/2017-07-13/15-year-old-graduates-from-university-with-first-class-degree/|website=ITV News|language=en|access-date=2020-05-17|archive-date=10 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010025804/http://www.itv.com/news/central/2017-07-13/15-year-old-graduates-from-university-with-first-class-degree/|url-status=live}}</ref>
